Question B-003-003-005.

Why the correct answer is right: The intermediate frequency (IF) filter provides adjacent-channel selectivity. It passes the wanted IF bandwidth and rejects nearby converted signals.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Mixer": The mixer translates frequencies and can create several products. It is not the main adjacent-channel rejection filter.
- sourceIndex 2: "Limiter": The limiter removes amplitude changes in frequency modulation (FM), not nearby-channel energy by bandwidth selection.
- sourceIndex 3: "Product detector": A product detector handles single-sideband (SSB) or continuous-wave (CW) recovery. Adjacent-channel rejection should happen before or around the IF filter.
